text.p: Shares of Lindeteves-Jacoberg Ltd (LJ) spurted on Monday on the back of good earnings prospects and the company's recently announced rights issue of loan stocks, dealers and analysts said.
At 0336 GMT, they had risen Singapore $0.13, or 5.7 percent, to S$2.41 on 205,000 shares after touching a new high of S$2.44 in early trade.
"We have been promoting the stock for some time, since it was S$0.75. Fundamentally it remains a buy," said Mano Sabnani, research director at DBS Investment Research.
He said he expected the company to grow at a annual compound rate of more than 20 percent in the next few years.
Good growth is seen from its power, environmental engineering and electric motor works businesses, he said.
Sabnani said he had put a fair value for the shares at S$2.60 based on expected earnings for the fiscal year ending March 1998.
LJ's recently announced rights issue of loan stock with free warrants had also shone more favour on the company, dealers and analysts said.
"Some investors are buying the shares for the loan stock and warrants as they stand to make a profit," said a dealer.
Sabnani said besides the "bonus" element of the loan stock and warrants, the exercise would lower the company's gearing and should help its bottom line.
He said he would be looking again at the value of LJ, with the possibility of raising it from S$2.60.
